Well, in this series that I'm taking you through about the four pillars of life, I'm finding it quite interesting myself because there are some surprising results.

A lot of the answers depend on where you live. For example, if you live in the United States, you know that this is true: the long path is much more fruitful than the quick fix. In many cultures, though, this is not true at all. For instance, in many of the nations that were part of the Soviet Union, the only way to get ahead is to find a quick, easy way to bypass the system.

So, as we go through this, keep in mind your cultural context.

As we established in the previous article, this set of topics is centered on the question of how much control we have over our lives. Specifically, we're asking whether our lives are the result of hard work and planning, or if they are the result of luck and external factors beyond our control.

The first of these questions was:

"Some people feel they have completely free choice and control over their lives, while other people feel that what they do has no real effect on what happens to them. Please use this scale where 1 means 'no choice at all' and 10 means 'a great deal of choice' to indicate how much freedom of choice and control you feel you have over the way your life turns out."

The answer for most countries is between 6.5 and 7.5.

Today, we're looking at the second question in this series:

"Which of these two statements do you tend to agree with?
A. In the long run, hard work usually brings a better life.
B. Hard work doesn't generally bring success - it's more a matter of luck and connections."

Again, you are asked to place yourself on a scale of 1 to 10, where 1 means you agree completely with statement A and 10 means you agree completely with statement B.

As with the previous question, most countries fall somewhere between 3 and 6 on the scale.

The lowest (most in favor of hard work) are:
1. United States (3.5)
2. Canada (3.7)
3. Australia (3.8)
4. New Zealand (3.8)
5. Great Britain (3.9)

The highest (most in favor of luck and connections) are:
1. Russia (5.9)
2. Ukraine (5.8)
3. Belarus (5.7)
4. Bulgaria (5.6)
5. Romania (5.5)

It's interesting to note that the countries that believe most in hard work are all English-speaking, Western democracies. The countries that believe most in luck and connections are all former communist states.

This makes sense, doesn't it? In a capitalist society, you are taught from a young age that if you work hard, you can achieve anything. In a communist society, the state controls everything, so your success is more dependent on your connections and luck.

But what about the countries in the middle?

The countries in the middle are a mix of Western and Eastern European countries, as well as countries from Asia and South America.

For example, France and Germany are both around 4.5. Japan is around 4.8. Brazil is around 5.1.

These countries seem to have a more balanced view of the role of hard work and luck in success. They recognize that hard work is important, but they also realize that luck and connections can play a significant role.

So, what does this tell us?

It tells us that our beliefs about hard work and luck are shaped by our culture and the society we live in. If we live in a society that rewards hard work, we are more likely to believe that hard work leads to success. If we live in a society where success is more dependent on connections and luck, we are more likely to believe that.

But it also tells us that there is no one "right" answer. Both hard work and luck play a role in success. The key is to find the right balance for yourself.

If you believe too much in hard work, you may become frustrated when things don't go your way. If you believe too much in luck, you may not put in the effort required to succeed.

The best approach is to work hard, but also to be aware of the role that luck and connections can play. By doing so, you can increase your chances of success and also be more resilient when things don't go as planned.

So, where do you fall on the scale? Do you believe that hard work usually brings a better life, or that success is more a matter of luck and connections?
